label: see also
type: MAPPING RECORD, NOT A MINTED PREDICATE. Every structural Markdown link between two documentation pages is extracted as seeAlso, which maps directly onto rdfs:seeAlso. Object is a PAGE ID, never a concept.
note: Filed in round 11 because seeAlso is by an order of magnitude the most-used predicate in the corpus - 425 of 2991 relations - and had no registry record at all, being a reuse rather than a mint. Two consequences worth writing down. (1) Nobody should mint a link predicate; this record exists so that the answer is on disk rather than in the skill prose. (2) It distorts recurrence counting: because seeAlso objects are pages, a naive object-recurrence query over the corpus returns a ranked list of popular DOCUMENTATION PAGES and presents it as a list of concept-promotion candidates. Round 11's first aggregation did exactly that and put search:customize-index (a page) above every real concept. Exclude seeAlso before counting concept recurrence.
